text:
incident-bot: ALERT: routing-latency-euw > p99 threshold. 10:52 UTC. Region: eu-west-1. p95 ~ 800ms -> p95 2.1s, p99 6.8s, streaming stall rate increased. Autogenerated page created: https://go.incidents/INC-7642 : siren

anna-oncall: seeing the same in the dashboard, p99 spike started ~10:45. Streaming requests show long stalls at router handoff step.

ryan-sre: oncall here, joining bridge. Assigned page INC-7642. First triage: probable routing policy misweighting — I see surge to a small shard set (hot partition).

sam-runtime: grabbing live logs from router pool euw1: `kubectl -n router logs router-euw1-3 --since=15m | grep Handoff` showed repeated `HandoffTimeout` and `policy_evaluate: shard_mismatch` lines.

anna-oncall: any recent rollouts? I didn't see a deployment in the last hour.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback was performed for routing-policy v12 -> v11 at 10:30 UTC in us-west-2 only. No eu-west rollouts recorded.

ryan-sre: ok. Dumping routing table snapshot and heatmap: `rbctl snapshot --region eu-west-1 --out /tmp/rb-euw-snap.json`

sam-runtime: attaching heatmap summary: hot shard id=shard-347 handling 18% of stream traffic, normal ~1.2%. Looks like a hash skew after a seed change in policy v12 but why only euw1?

jess-cs: customer impact: CS saw 7 customer tickets in the last 20m reporting stalled streaming sessions and long waits. Most on eu-west-1. ETA communicated to affected users?

maria-product: flagged for potential SLA breach. We need an external customer message ASAP.

anna-oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) reweight routing policy to move traffic off shard-347, 2) force rehash seed to previous value, 3) enable eager fallback to stateless model variant. Which is fastest?

ryan-sre: reweight is fastest. Plan: update policy weights for eu-west-1 to reduce weight for shard-347 by 90% and increase fallback pool. Command:

```
routerctl policy update --region eu-west-1 --policy-id rp-main --set weight.shard-347=0.1 --set weight.fallback=1.9
```

I'll run in 2m and monitor.

sam-runtime: watch KV cache eviction and in-flight KV lengths; streaming stalls usually recover when in-flight drops. I'll add quick health check to mark nodes with >500ms handoff as unhealthy.

anna-oncall: executing voice bridge + page notes. @ryan-sre go ahead.

ryan-sre: running update now. `routerctl: success` — policy update propagated to eu-west-1 controllers.

ops-bot: ops-audit: policy change by ryan-sre at 10:59 UTC (INC-7642).

anna-oncall: p95/p99 graph - refresh in progress... p95 dropped from 2.1s -> 780ms within 90s, p99 down from 6.8s -> 1.7s. Streaming stall rate cut from 8% -> 1.5%. Nice.

jess-cs: pushing status update to affected customers: "We are seeing elevated streaming latency in EU-WEST-1 and have routed traffic away from an overloaded shard. Partial mitigation in place; monitoring. Next update in 30m."

maria-product: please also add note we have started a post-incident investigation; SLO impact being assessed.

sam-runtime: quick follow-up: root cause looks like a regression in hashing seed selection introduced in rp-engine v12 config parser; it caused a small set of high-frequency keys to map to shard-347 consistently. Two fixes: revert seed behavior (short-term) and add deterministic test for seed drift (long-term).

ryan-sre: agreed. Opening followup ticket: RT-1429 for config parser fix + test harness.

anna-oncall: rolling handoff to oncall eu-night at 17:00 UTC. Notes attached to the page: mitigation performed (weight adjust), p95/p99 recovered, customer notifications sent, follow-up RT-1429 assigned to eng-runtime.

ops-bot: incident-bot: bridge closed at 11:06 UTC. Final triage: regional routing policy bug -> hot shard -> tail latency spike. Severity: P2 (customer-impacting SLO).

ryan-sre: leftover tasks: 1) ensure rollback path for rp-engine v12 is documented, 2) add canary that simulates heavy-key distribution, 3) confirm no other regions hit. I'll run a cross-regional heatmap query and post results in thread before handoff.

sam-runtime: here's quick query output (summarized): `regions scanned: eu-west-1: hot shard found; other regions: normal distribution.`

jess-cs: I'll keep monitoring support queue and surface any escalations.

anna-oncall: thanks all. Leaving incident notes in INC-7642. Handoff complete. :white_check_mark:
